name: Break the Code
summary: Logical deduction game where players use question cards to deduce hidden numbered and colored tiles.
rules_text: Each player hides 5 tiles (4 in 4-player) behind a screen, sorted ascending, red before blue for same number. 20 tiles containing numbers 0-9 in two colors are shuffled and dealt. 21 question cards are shuffled; six are face up. On your turn you must either ask one face-up question card or attempt to guess. If you ask, your opponent(s) must answer truthfully according to the card (e.g., where is a number, where are same colors adjacent, where are sequential numbers). Asked cards are discarded and replaced from the deck. In 2-player you guess opponent's 5 tiles in order; if wrong you continue, if right you win but opponent gets one final guess chance, otherwise tie if deck runs out. In 3-4 players there is a central pool of 4-5 hidden tiles; players ask and all opponents answer (all shared in 4-player), and any player may once per game secretly check and claim the central tiles; wrong guess eliminates you from asking.
rating_reason: Pure logical deduction with number tiles, perfect hidden information game
